column1: # THE LIVE CATALOGUE, AS THE PROBE HARNESS MUST FIND IT.
# WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR. scripts/probes/escrow_concurrency.sh lifts function
# TEXT out of supabase/migrations/*.sql by scanning for
# `create or replace function` and taking the last definition of each name. A
# `drop function` is neither a create nor a replace, so a verb dropped in
# production goes on passing here against a body that no longer exists
# anywhere. The same hole swallows a signature changed, a body rewritten by a
# do-block the harness does not replay, a body edited straight against the
# database, and a migration written but never applied.
# So the harness stops trusting the migrations on their own. After it loads
# the lifted bodies into its scratch cluster it reads ITS OWN pg_proc and
# compares it, row by row, against this file. A disagreement in the CODE stops
# the run before the smoke check, because a probe running the wrong body is
# worse than no probe at all.
# WHY THERE ARE TWO HASHES, AND WHICH ONE STOPS THE RUN.
#   body_sha256 is sha256 of prosrc exactly as stored.
#   code_sha256 is sha256 of prosrc with SQL comments removed, trailing
#   whitespace stripped and blank lines collapsed.
#   The gate is code_sha256, because that is the difference that changes what
#   the database does. A body_sha256 that moves while code_sha256 holds is
#   reported as a LOUD WARNING naming every function, and the run continues.
#   THIS IS NOT A THEORETICAL DISTINCTION. The first real run of this guard,
#   on 23 September 2026, found FIVE functions whose live body differs from
#   the migration text in this repository: private.compute_fee,
#   private.notify, private.move_into_pot, private.escrow_invariants_check and
#   private.pay_booking_from_wallet. In every one of the five the live copy is
#   the same code with its `--` comments stripped out. Who stripped them is
#   NOT KNOWN and is written up in ledger section 63 as unexplained. Refusing
#   to run over a missing comment would have meant the guard was deleted
#   within a day; passing over a changed statement would have meant it was
#   worthless. Hence two hashes.
#   WHAT THE GATE CANNOT SEE, said plainly. Comment stripping is applied to
#   both sides, so a `--` sequence INSIDE a string literal is removed from
#   both and a difference after it would be missed. Nothing in these thirty
#   two bodies has one.
# WHY THE HASH IS OF prosrc AND NOT OF THE MIGRATION TEXT. Postgres reformats
# what `pg_get_functiondef` prints but stores the body between the dollar
# quotes BYTE FOR BYTE. Hashing prosrc compares two catalogues rather than two
# spellings of one thing.
# HOW TO REFRESH IT. Read pg_proc on the live project with the query recorded
# in ledger section 63 and rewrite this file. The harness does not generate it
# and cannot: the machine the harness runs on has no route to the project,
# which is the same wall P-7's HTTP half is behind.
# WHAT IT IS NOT, AND THE `acl` COLUMN IS NOT COMPARED. The scratch cluster
# has no `anon`, no `authenticated` and no `service_role` at all, and the
# harness lifts bodies rather than grants, so its catalogue can say nothing
# about privilege and a comparison would be theatre. `acl` is recorded here so
# that a reader can see what the live grants were when this file was taken and
# cross-check it against P-7, which is the probe that actually proves the
# EXECUTE layer. This file does not stand in for it.
